reviewBoundary: These are review-ready drafts, not verified publication chapters. No machine setting, safety procedure, or material processing value may be inferred from them.

sourceSeeds.title: Plastics — Injection moulding of test specimens of thermoplastic materials — Part 1: General principles, and moulding of multipurpose and bar test specimens
sourceSeeds.scope: General injection-moulding principles, consistent process-parameter descriptions and reproducible reporting. ISO confirms the 2017 edition remains current after review in 2022.

chapters.applicability: General thermoplastic injection-moulding concepts only. Actual process windows depend on the material grade, machine, mould, part requirements and applicable site controls.

sections.title: The process in one sentence
sections.text: Injection moulding is a repeating sequence: prepare the melt, push a controlled shot into a closed mould, let the part form and become stable enough to handle, then open the mould and remove it ready for the next cycle.

sections.title: What the process must achieve
sections.text: Getting plastic into the cavity is only the start. A production process has to make the required shape and properties repeatedly, while staying inside the real limits of the material, machine, mould and safety system.

sections.title: Why settings are not universal
sections.text: There is no set of moulding conditions that travels unchanged from job to job. Even standards written for repeatable test specimens recognise that conditions depend on the material. Production adds another layer: part geometry, mould design, machine capability and the actual quality requirements all matter.

sections.title: How to think like a process engineer
sections.text: Start with the part result you need, then work back to the machine inputs that create it. Watch what the material and cavity are telling you, record the conditions that matter, and when you need to learn cause and effect, change one justified variable at a time.

chapters.applicability: Conceptual cycle model. Controller names, available phases and transition methods vary by machine and process.

sections.title: Prepare the next shot
sections.text: While one part is being made, the plasticising unit is already preparing what comes next. The screw rotates and moves back as material is conveyed, heated and mixed into the next shot. That means material preparation and thermal history still matter while the mould is shut and the current part is cooling.

sections.title: Fill the cavity
sections.text: The screw moves forward and drives melt through the nozzle, feed system and gate into the cavity. The machine is commanding motion, but the resistance of the flow path decides how much pressure is needed to achieve it. A pressure value on the machine screen is useful evidence, not a direct reading of cavity pressure.

sections.title: Transfer and pack
sections.text: Near the end of filling, the process changes jobs: it moves from driving the flow front toward controlling post-fill pressure. Packing can compensate for contraction while the gate and part can still respond. Where to transfer and how to pack have to be established on the actual moulded system; they are not percentages or pressures to copy from another job.

sections.title: Cool and eject
sections.text: The part stays in the mould until it is stable enough to open and eject without unacceptable damage or deformation. How long that takes depends on the material, geometry, mould-temperature distribution and the way heat is being removed.

sections.title: Treat the cycle as an interacting system
sections.text: The controller may show neat, separate phases, but the physics overlaps. Plasticising can be happening while the part cools, and the thermal or pressure history created in one phase can change what happens in the next. When a process drifts, follow the whole cycle rather than staring at one screen value.

chapters.applicability: General injection-moulding-machine architecture. Exact guarding, drives, controls and component names depend on the machine manufacturer and configuration.

sections.title: Injection unit
sections.text: The injection unit takes in raw material, turns it into a usable melt, meters the shot and then drives that melt toward the mould. Most reciprocating-screw machines share familiar elements such as the feed system, heated barrel, screw, non-return function and nozzle, although the details of their design and control vary.

sections.title: Clamping unit
sections.text: The clamp carries the mould through closing, clamping, opening and the motions associated with releasing the part. How it does that depends on the machine: hydraulic, electric and hybrid designs use different mechanical arrangements, so similar-looking controller commands can sit on very different hardware.

sections.title: Control and energy systems
sections.text: The controller coordinates motion, temperature, pressure, timing, alarms and interlocks, but the screen is only one view of the machine. Behind it are electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, thermal and stored-energy hazards whose safe state cannot be judged from process values alone.

sections.title: Use the machine documentation
sections.text: When the task involves setup limits, guarding, isolation, maintenance or permitted operation, go to the manufacturer's instructions and the site's approved procedure. This Book can explain how the process works; it cannot replace the machine-specific safety and operating documents.

chapters.applicability: General mould-component concepts and terminology. Actual mould construction varies widely and may omit or add systems described here.

sections.title: The mould creates the part-forming space
sections.text: The core and cavity surfaces create the shape of the part, but a working mould has more to do than define geometry. It has to accept the melt, manage heat, stay aligned under load, open in the intended sequence and release the moulding without damaging either the part or the tool.

sections.title: Feed system
sections.text: In a cold-runner mould the feed path may include a sprue, runners and one or more gates; a hot runner changes how that melt is carried and controlled. The gate deserves particular attention because it is both a restriction and a process boundary. Its size and thermal condition can change filling and what happens after fill.

sections.title: Guidance, support and ejection
sections.text: Locating, guiding and support components keep the mould aligned and carry the loads produced during the cycle. Once the part is ready to come off the tool, the ejection system supplies the release motion. Do not assume the arrangement from a generic diagram; identify how the actual mould is built.

sections.title: Temperature-control system
sections.text: Cooling or temperature-control circuits move heat into or out of the tool. Their layout, flow condition and local heat load can create noticeably different surface temperatures across one mould, which is why the temperature-control-unit setpoint should never be treated as the temperature of every cavity surface.

chapters.applicability: Awareness only. It is not a lockout/tagout procedure, machine-specific safe system of work, guarding instruction or authorisation to enter a hazardous area.

sections.title: Safety is a system boundary
sections.text: An injection-moulding machine puts hazardous motion, hot surfaces and material, pressure, electricity and other stored energy in the same working area. Safe operation depends on the machine's engineered safeguards, its actual condition, the approved procedures around it and people who are competent for the task.

sections.title: A stopped screen is not an isolation
sections.text: A machine that is not moving is not automatically safe to enter or work on. A cycle stop, an open guard or a quiet controller does not prove that hazardous energy has been isolated or dissipated.

sections.title: Guarding and interlocks are safety functions
sections.text: Guards and interlocks are part of the safety system, not obstacles to production. If a safeguard prevents the job you want to do, that is the point to use the approved machine- and site-specific method, not to defeat or work around the safeguard.

sections.title: When this Book must stop
sections.text: If the job involves entering a danger zone, isolating energy, dealing with stored energy, maintenance, an abnormal machine condition or uncertainty about a safeguard, stop using this Book as the procedure. Follow the machine manufacturer's instructions, the site's authorised safety system and competent supervision.
